items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Daniel Humair, one of the besst drummer in town, my friend, the sax tenor Guy Lafitte

ctx.x: I went back to play at the Trois Mailletz. I had been angry for some time with Madame Calvé, but decided to forget the difference. Past was past, and it's nice sometimes to play in a club. Another club where I started to play was the Caveau de la Huchette, also situated in the Latin Quarter, which had been bought by Danny Doris, the vibraphonist with whom I had worked quite a few times. The atmosphere of the Huchette was more easier going than at the Trois Mailletz, where people came more to listen to music. In…

A famous well known French composer and singer, Guy Béart, contacted me. He had a T.V. programme called "Bienvenue" which means "Welcome" to Guy Béart. He wss having that programme about twice a month, andhe was inviting all kinds of personalities for his show. He told me that he wanted to make a show called "Bienvenue to American artists", and asked me if I was willing to contact the American musicians available in Paris. I rang Mickey Baker, guitarist, Kenny Clark, drummer, Art Simmons, piano, Benny Water,…

We were all very excited to be with Duke. He came on the T.V. set at 5 p.m., dressed in a light blue costume(it was in July). Guy Béart introduced him to the audience, because Guy Béart always had his emission semi-public with personalities, artists, guests, press, and a lot of beautiful girls, who were engaged especially to add more class to the show.
